name: Abyssal Scroll
description: Abyssal Scroll is a world of water without end. Its ocean averages fourteen kilometers in depth, with abyssal trenches plunging to nearly sixty, and no landmass breaks the surface anywhere on the planet. The water itself shifts through deep indigo to near-black depending on depth, with vast blooms of bioluminescent organisms creating patterns visible from orbit—swirling scripts of light that scroll across the surface with the currents. A permanent hurricane system dominates the southern hemisphere, its eye large enough to swallow a small moon.

The dense atmosphere presses down on the ocean surface with a weight that makes the water eerily still between storm systems. Beneath the waves, the silence is absolute in the upper layers, giving way to a deep-frequency thrumming near the geothermal vents that the research team has termed 'the planet's heartbeat.' The bioluminescent fauna range from microscopic plankton to creatures of staggering size—sonar has detected organisms exceeding two kilometers in length in the deepest trenches.

A research outpost floats on the surface near the equator, anchored by cables to a seamount four kilometers below. The team has cataloged over twelve thousand species in six years and estimates they have documented less than one percent of the planet's biodiversity. A persistent low-frequency signal rises from somewhere in the deepest trench, too regular to be geological, too complex to be simple biological communication. No submersible has yet reached the signal's source.

Abyssal Scroll's pharmaceutical potential alone makes it one of the most valuable oceanic worlds in the sector, with three compounds already in medical trials showing extraordinary promise. But the signal from the deep has attracted a different kind of interest—xenolinguists who believe it may represent a form of communication from an intelligence that evolved entirely in a lightless, pressurized environment. The next deep-trench expedition is being assembled, and its findings may redefine what it means for a world to be 'uninhabited.'
